label: accepted

evidence.V1: Front reads as a classic diamond (flat-topped crown over a pointed pavilion), top view as a clean elongated octagon, and the 3/4 silhouette as a gem. All three read at 64 px. The narrow end looks slightly rounded in the 3/4 outline, but it is still unmistakable.
evidence.V2: Big: crown and pavilion masses. Medium: a lighter table, a stepped ring of crown facets and the girdle band. Small: chamfer lines and corner facets. The table, crown and pavilion value steps make the tiers obvious.
evidence.V3: A confident chunky stylised gem: a tall stepped crown, a compact pavilion ending in a sharp-ish culet, and a footprint elongated about 0.95 x 0.80. It is not a stiff primitive. Symmetry error is X 0.0 / Y 0.0, the front outline is symmetric and the origin is centred.
evidence.V4: Even chamfers run along every crown step, the table rim and the girdle, and catch light as thin highlight lines in the studio close-ups. They are consistent across crown and pavilion, with no razor edges and nothing blobby.
evidence.V5: The close-ups (crown and pavilion, studio and flat) show crisp planar facets with no pinches, seams, z-fighting or overlapping caps. The gate shows A17/A18 pass, 0 flipped faces and 0 cap overlaps. Facet gradients come only from the one-sided Workbench light.
evidence.V6: One hue in three values: light table, mid crown, dark pavilion, as the kit intends. The colourways (crimson, royal) keep the same value structure.
evidence.V7: 286 tris against the small-class target of 600 (ceiling 1500), which is lean for a chamfered step-cut.
evidence.V8: One white material (LF_VertexColor, SmoothPlastic) with vertex colours, one hue in up to 3 values, chamfered edges with smooth shading. It sits beside the Coin_02 anchor without a visible clash.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Pickup with CanCollide off, CanTouch on, CollisionFidelity Box, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white for vertex colours, SmoothPlastic, origin at centre. All correct for a collectible.

evidence.V1: Reads as a cut gem at 64 px from every view: front is a classic crown-over-pointed-pavilion outline, top is a clean elongated octagon step-cut, three-quarter/silhouette keep the flat crown plus culet point; A15 symmetry error X/Y = 0.0 and the front outline is mirror-even.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: big crown vs deep pavilion, medium octagonal table plus step facets ring, small chamfer bands on every facet edge; no uniform noise.
evidence.V3: Confident stylised gem: chunky raised crown with broad table and a deep tapered pavilion, rounder and more appealing than plain primitives; centred on origin, no seating parts to fail.
evidence.V4: Consistent thin chamfers on all crown, girdle and pavilion edges that catch light as highlight lines (visible in crown studio and flat close-ups), no razor edges.
evidence.V5: Mostly clean, but smooth shading bleeds across the chamfers so several facets carry gradients instead of reading flat: a soft light streak at the left crown step corner in the three-quarter/crown close-up, a horizontal gradient band across the front crown facets, and curved light-dark gradients on the left pavilion facets toward the culet in the pavilion close-up.
evidence.V6: One hue in 3 disciplined values (light table, mid crown, dark pavilion); the crimson/royal colourways keep the same value structure.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material with vertex colours, chamfered edges and smooth shading, one hue in up to 3 values: matches the kit; faces read slightly softer than the Coin_02 anchor's crisp flat faces.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, Box fidelity, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin centre.

evidence.V1: Front outline is a symmetric crown + pointed pavilion (A15 X/Y error 0.0), the three-quarter silhouette still reads as a cut gem, and the top view reads as an octagonal cushion; recognisable at 64 px from every angle.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: big = crown vs pavilion mass; medium = table, ring of bezel facets, girdle band, pavilion main facets; small = corner facets and chamfer lines. The pavilion is the plainest part but its facet breaks still read.
evidence.V3: Chunky stylised proportion: a shallow crown about 1/3 of the height over a deep pointed pavilion, with a slightly elongated top (0.95 x 0.80 studs); reads as a confident stylised gem, not a stiff primitive.
evidence.V4: Thin chamfers run consistently along the table rim, the bezel edges and the girdle, and catch light as bright lines in the studio close-ups, matching the kit's soft-edge look.
evidence.V5: Minor: some planar facets shade unevenly under Workbench studio light, so smoothed normals bleed across faces that should be flat. There is a soft wide highlight smear at the bezel/table corner in the crown close-up, a horizontal light streak across the crown in the front view, and top-to-bottom gradients on the left crown and pavilion facets. No seams, pinches or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: One hue in three values (light table, mid crown, dark pavilion) with strong value contrast; the crimson and royal colourways keep the same value structure.
evidence.V7: 286 tris against the small-class target of 600 (ceiling 1500), so well under target.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material with vertex colours, a single kit hue in up to 3 values, chamfered edges and smooth shading; matches the kit.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, Box fidelity, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin at centre.

artifacts: Minor: at the narrow ends of the octagon the small corner facets and chamfers blend into a soft gradient in the studio close-ups (crown close-up left end), so the facet edges read less crisply there. Not a defect.
Minor: the culet tip looks slightly blunted in the front and pavilion close-up views.
Smooth-shading gradients inside facets: specular streak at the left crown step corner (three-quarter and crown studio close-up)
Horizontal gradient band across the crown facets in the front view
Curved light-dark gradients on the left pavilion facets near the culet (pavilion studio close-up)
Smoothed normals bleed across planar facets: soft highlight smear at the bezel/table corner (crown studio close-up) and gradient shading inside crown and pavilion facets that should shade flat
top_fixes: Sharpen the narrow-end corner facets (narrower chamfers or a slightly larger corner facet) so the step-cut stays crisp at the ends and the 3/4 outline reads less rounded.
Add a little more definition to the pavilion (for example a second tier of pavilion facets or a stronger value split) so the lower half carries the same detail density as the crown.
Bring the culet to a cleaner point so the front-view diamond silhouette ends crisply.

Make each facet shade flat: use weighted normals (face-area/strength) or mark the facet-to-chamfer edges so smoothing stays inside the chamfer bands and each crown/pavilion facet reads as one even plane
Tighten the culet and pavilion facet junctions so the lower point reads crisper at small sizes
Make each planar facet shade flat: split normals at every facet edge (sharp edges / weighted normals with face-strength) so the chamfers carry the highlight and the facets themselves stay uniform
Add a bit more definition to the pavilion (one clear lighter value step or a visible keel line on the main facets) so the lower half doesn't read as one dark mass at small sizes
